question: How does Principal Component Analysis (PCA) contribute to dimensionality reduction in machine learning?

message.content:
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) contributes to dimensionality reduction primarily by transforming high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional space while preserving as much variance as possible. It achieves this by identifying the principal components—orthogonal axes that represent the directions of maximum variance—ranked by how much data they explain.

The process involves computing the covariance matrix of the features and performing eigendecomposition to find these axes. By selecting only the top $k$ components, you can project the original data onto a reduced subspace. This effectively removes redundant or noisy features that contribute little to the overall structure of the data, reducing complexity and often improving model performance by mitigating the curse of dimensionality.
